newsitem.title: CHINA: China takes central control of stock exchanges.
newsitem.headline: China takes central control of stock exchanges.

text.p: China's State Council has ordered the country's top securities watchdog, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, to take direct control over its two stock exchanges in Shanghai and Shenzhen, state media said on Friday.
"This is to further strengthen the management of the stock markets and to smooth the management system of the stock exchanges," the Financial News said.
The decision would protect the interests of investors and ensure greater stability, the newspaper said.
The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges already effectively cover the markets throughout the country, it said.
"The rapid expansion and scale of development force the need to strengthen unified central control," the newspaper said quoting officials close to the decision by the State Council, or cabinet.
The decision to take over control from the centre would push the markets in the direction of "legal, supervised, self-disciplined and regulated" systems, it said.
The presidents and vice presidents of the two exchanges would be directly appointed by the regulatory commission, it said.
It announced the recent appointment of Tu Guangshao, formerly in charge of the transactions department of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), as head of the Shanghai market.
It did not say whether the head of the Shenzhen market had been removed, but informed sources have said they expected Gui Minjie, head of the international department of the CSRC, to take over.

The move, the latest in a series of measures by Beijing in recent months to crack down on what it sees as excessive speculation on its stock exchanges, was expected to send a chill through the markets.
China's markets have shed about 30 percent in the last three months after Beijing clamped down in mid-May to end overheating and excessive speculation.

However, the Shenzhen hard currency B index leapt 13.78 points to its 10 percent limit-up level of 151.22 on Thursday while turnover more than doubled as foreign and Hong Kong investors bought shares seen as underpriced compared with H shares listed in Hong Kong.
Shanghai's B index closed the day up 7.227 points or 9.86 percent -- near the 10 percent daily limit -- to 80.496 points.
Shenzhen's domestic currency A share index also gained on Thursday but with less gusto, rising 11.15 points, or 3.01 percent, to 382.01.
The Shanghai A index closed up 48.325 points or 4.13 percent to 1,218.933 points.
